newsitem.title: DUBAI: Safety expert says data should explain India crash.
newsitem.headline: Safety expert says data should explain India crash.

text.p: An international aviation safety expert said on Wednesday India's recovery of the flight data recorders meant the cause of the world's worst mid-air collision might be clear within two weeks.

"If, on the assumption that the flight data recorders can be easily read, I would imagine that you would begin to have some information in less than two weeks," said Stuart Matthews, chairman of the U.S.-based Flight Safety Foundation (FSF).

"But whether they release this information to the press, I do not know, because different countries have different rules," he told Reuters on the sidelines of an international meeting on aviation safety which opened in Dubai on Monday.
Tuesday's mid-air collision between a Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo jet and a Kazakh cargo plane near New Delhi killed some 350 people.

Matthews said two top Saudi officials at the meeting left for India late on Tuesday to help in the investigation. "Black box" flight and cockpit voice recorders from both aircraft were found on Wednesday.
Matthews said a misunderstanding on altitude or pilot or air traffic control error were among potential causes of the mid-air collision but it was all guess work.
"The first idea is that one or both pilots of the aircraft made a mistake and one aircraft went too low and the other one came up too high, so they should have been separated.

"The second one is that the air traffic control people made a mistake and directed them on a crossing path, so one was told to go down and the other was told to go up and they hit each other in the middle.
"And the third possibility is that somebody had an incorrect altimeter, or the possibility of confusion in the units which have been used as Russians tend to use metres and Saudis use feet," he said.
